summary.text: The nervous system is the part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by sending signals to and from different parts of its body.
It detects changes in the environment that affect the body, then works together with the endocrine system to respond to them.
In vertebrates it has two main parts: the central nervous system, made of the brain and spinal cord, and the peripheral nervous system, made mainly of nerves.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Arose in wormlike organisms about 550 to 600 million years ago

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: Few hundred cells in simplest worms; 300 billion in elephants

facts.label: Who studies it
facts.value: Neuroscience studies it; neurology studies its disorders

items.prompt: A person sits calmly on a couch, fully relaxed. Which part of the autonomic nervous system is mostly active?
items.explain: The parasympathetic system is the one activated when an organism is in a relaxed state, while the sympathetic system handles emergencies.

items.prompt: A driver slams the brakes to avoid a crash and feels a surge of energy. Which system just switched on to mobilize it?
items.explain: The sympathetic nervous system is activated in emergencies to mobilize energy.

items.prompt: You touch a hot mug and information races from your hand toward your central nervous system. Which nerves carry it?
items.explain: Nerves carrying information from the body to the CNS are sensory (afferent) nerves; motor nerves carry signals away from the brain.

items.prompt: A biologist compares a jellyfish with a cat. How does the jellyfish's nervous system differ in layout?

options.label: It is a brain with one cord and nerves branching off
It has no nervous system because it is so simple
It is a single thick nerve running through the body
It is a diffuse nerve net of loosely connected cells

items.explain: Jellyfish are radially symmetric, and their nervous system is a diffuse nerve net. Most other animals have a brain, a central cord and nerves radiating from them.

items.prompt: Neurons do the signalling, but other cells give them structural and metabolic support. What are those helper cells called?
items.explain: Glial cells, or glia, are the non-neuronal cells that support neurons structurally and metabolically.

items.prompt: A surgeon says an injury affects the central nervous system. Which pair of structures is the central nervous system made of?

options.label: The brain and the spinal cord

items.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, while the nerves belong to the peripheral nervous system.
